extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians preparing and submitting research papers to the Canadian Mathematical Bulletin (authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Author instructions and publication policies for preparing and submitting research manuscripts to the Canadian Mathematical Bulletin, covering formatting, submission, peer review, copyright, and post-acceptance steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: A research paper submitted to the Canadian Mathematical Bulletin (Bulletin) should be at most 18 pages long. Papers greater than 20 pages should instead be submitted to the Canadian Journal of Mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the paper does not exceed 18 pages for the Bulletin; if it is over 20 pages target the Canadian Journal of Mathematics instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers may be written in English or in French.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either English or French is acceptable; ensure language choice is consistent and clear throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript finality and conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: It is vital that authors take care to ensure that the manuscript is in final form and that the paper conforms to the following specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should prepare a submission-ready manuscript that adheres to all specified formatting and content requirements before submitting (see subsequent criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: First page contents and abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The first page should contain a short descriptive title, the name(s) of the author(s) followed by an abstract, not exceeding 200 words, which can be read independently of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise descriptive title and an independent abstract ≤200 words that summarizes the paper’s content; place authors' names on the first page as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract/page should be followed by the Mathematics Subject Classification Number for the primary and secondary subjects of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include primary and secondary MSC codes immediately after the abstract to identify subject areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author affiliation and contact on last page
rubrics_metrics.description: The institutional affiliation and complete address of each author (including e-mail) should appear at the bottom of the last page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place full affiliation and complete postal address plus email for every author on the last page (not the first).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference style and DOI inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations should be given in an alphabetical bibliography at the end of the paper. The list of references should use the standard abbreviations issued by Mathematical Reviews (MR) and should include the DOI whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare an alphabetical reference list using MR standard abbreviations; include DOIs where available (use Crossref to find DOIs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Bulletin class file
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a specific class file for Bulletin papers which is available here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to use the Journal’s LaTeX class file for formatting; obtain and apply the provided .cls to conform to layout expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format and system
rubrics_metrics.description: When the manuscript is in its final form, it should be submitted online, in PDF form, by clicking the Submit your article link. The EditFlow service is used to manage communications between the editors and authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a PDF of the final manuscript via the journal’s online submission system (EditFlow). Ensure you have the required account for the submission system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are reviewed for suitability, importance of findings, and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the paper addresses an appropriate topic for the Bulletin, presents findings of sufficient importance, and is clearly written; these are primary screening criteria before refereeing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee selection and anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: After screening, papers are sent to academic referee(s), unknown to the author(s), expert in the appropriate subject area and carefully chosen by the Editorial Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review is conducted by anonymous expert referees chosen by the Editorial Board; authors should not identify or recommend referees in a way that compromises anonymity unless the submission system requests it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referees' role in verification and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees verify the scientific findings and may improve the clarity of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect referees to check correctness and may request revisions to improve exposition; respond thoroughly to referee reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright Assignment Form (CAF)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author will be required to complete and sign the Copyright Assignment Form (CAF) as part of the submission process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon acceptance, complete and sign the CAF to assign copyright to the Canadian Mathematical Society (CMS) so the CMS can legally publish the paper online and in print (see standard terms and conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional Gold Open Access (APC) option
rubrics_metrics.description: When completing the CAF, the authors are also given the option to designate the paper for full public access in exchange for a one-time paper processing fee. If the author decline Gold Open Access, the paper will be published using the traditional publishing model (available only to subscribers for the first five years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must decide on Gold Open Access at CAF completion and pay the required fee if choosing OA; otherwise the paper will be subscriber-restricted for five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of source files after acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Cambridge University Press (the Publisher on behalf of the CMS) with a complete set of the most recent LaTeX source files (and any supplementary files required, such as figures or macros) and a PDF version of the resulting manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After acceptance supply clean, complete LaTeX source and all supplementary files plus a PDF; ensure figures and macros are included and compileable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted Manuscript (AM) posting and DOI assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: After Cambridge receives the source files and copyright assignment, the submitted manuscript will be assigned a permanent DOI and temporary headers and footers will be added. This version of the paper will be posted to the Bulletin's website in the 'Accepted Manuscripts' (AM) section and also emailed to the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted manuscripts are posted quickly in AM form with a DOI and temporary formatting to provide early access; authors will receive the AM via email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green Open Access encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: We encourage authors to post a copy of the Accepted Manuscript version of the paper in arXiv, on their own institutional repositories, on other non-commercial repositories, or on their personal web sites in place of any previous versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are permitted and encouraged to self-archive the Accepted Manuscript (e.g., on arXiv or institutional repositories) under the publisher’s standard terms and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyediting, typesetting and proofs process
rubrics_metrics.description: Cambridge will copyedit and typeset the paper to finalize it for official online and print publication and ensure that the paper conforms to the layout and style of the publication. In some cases, the process may change the content of the paper (for example, to re-word portions or to improve clarity). During the process, a 'Proof' copy is sent to the communicating author for comments and corrections. Once corrections have been processed, the paper is reviewed for final approval and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect editorial copyediting and typesetting; authors will receive proofs to correct errors and should return corrections promptly. Be aware copyediting may alter wording for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: FirstView publication and official publication status
rubrics_metrics.description: When the paper is in final typeset form, the paper will be made available on the Bulletin’s web site FirstView section. The AM version will be simultaneously removed. Note that a Bulletin research paper is considered officially published when it appears online in FirstView.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final, citable, official publication occurs upon appearance in FirstView; the Accepted Manuscript is replaced by the Version of Record at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print issue assignment and metadata updates
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Bulletin paper is included in a print issue, the online version is updated slightly to include the volume and issue number and the page numbers are re-assigned relative to the volume/issue. On the Bulletin’s web site, the paper moves from the FirstView section into the area dedicated to the new issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final bibliographic details (volume, issue, page numbers) are assigned when the paper is placed in a print issue and the online record is updated accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact for further enquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Further Enquiries and Other Issues: Please contact cmb-editors@cms.math.ca.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided email address for queries about submission, editorial decisions, or publication processes.
